headline: On October 26, 1977: Last natural smallpox case in Somalia
captionCards: His story highlights the success of global vaccination campaigns
instagramCaption:
Ali Maow Maalin, a Somali hospital cook, develops a rash.
In October 1977, Ali Maow Maalin, a hospital cook and health worker from Merca, Somalia, was the last person to naturally contract Variola minor smallpox. Despite many contacts, no one else developed the disease, thanks to an aggressive containment campaign. Smallpox was declared eradicated globally by the WHO in 1979. Maalin later worked on polio eradication until his death in 2013. 
Why is this still important today? It shows the power of global vaccination efforts.
